title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: A 15-handle daily RSI in a Stage 4 liquidation is not a buy signal—it is a warning that institutional supply has overwhelmed every moving-average floor and that patience for a true Stage 1 base is the only edge.
epigraph.author: Technical & Tape Desk

web_blocks.html: NVIDIA Corporation is in a severe Weinstein Stage 4 (Markdown) breakdown. As of November 20, 2026, NVDA closed at $125.53, plunging -14.01% on the day, -26.12% over one week, and -43.19% over one month [23]. TradingView's 1W (-26.12%) and 1M (-43.19%) returns differ slightly from Finviz's trailing-window returns (-22.92% 1W / -40.85% 1M in [S9.1]) due to window and cut-off convention. The stock now sits -48.42% below its $243.37 52-week high and barely 0.8% above its $124.50 52-week low [23]. The quantitative facts ledger tags NVDA Stage 1 (Basing) near 52-week lows. By contrast, the stage2_evaluation trend screen classifies it as STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN) below falling 50D ($207.00), 200D ($203.35), and 30W ($208.02) averages. Every major daily, weekly, and 4-hour moving average is broken overhead. This triggers an AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN posture and a CAP_REJECTED technical timing gate.

The broader U.S. market backdrop offers zero tailwind for bottom-fishing. The S&P 500 is in a confirmed Downtrend with 10 distribution days over the past 25 sessions, only 35.8% of stocks above their 50-day moving average, and 40.3% above their 200-day moving average. Across 11 S&P sectors, just 1 sits above its 20-day moving average and 3 sit above their 50-day moving average. Against this fragile tape, NVDA's November 20 liquidation printed 630.31 million shares—2.80x its 30-day average volume of 224.75 million—confirming active institutional distribution rather than quiet retail selling.

web_blocks.html: Examining the multi-timeframe 1W / 1D / 4H tape clarifies why catching this knife is dangerous. On the weekly chart, NVDA sliced cleanly through its 10-week EMA ($188.46) and 30-week SMA ($208.02) on accelerating volume, pushing weekly RSI down to 25.01. On the daily chart, the stock gapped and cascaded past both Pivot S1 ($189.25) and Pivot S2 ($173.86), leaving a massive air pocket between $125.53 and $173.86. On the 4-hour chart, price remains 20.81% below its 4H 20-EMA ($158.52) with 4H RSI pinned at 14.95 and intraday_4h_turn: false.

At $125.53, NVDA is testing its 52-week low and major shelf at $124.50. While an oversold reflex bounce from $124.50 is possible, a true institutional bottom requires weeks of sideways Stage 1 basing—where 8.53% daily ATR compresses, 630M-share liquidation volume dries up, and price reclaims its 4H 20-EMA ($158.52) or builds a higher low in our $105.00–$118.00 demand zone. Until that stabilization occurs, both equity and unhedged calls carry unacceptable gap risk.

Stage 1 Base-Building Checklist (What Lifts CAP_REJECTED): Before our technical gate can upgrade from CAP_REJECTED to WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT execution in the $105.00–$118.00 zone, four observable tape conditions must align: (1) Volatility Compression—daily ATR(14) must contract from $10.71 (8.53% of CMP) back toward 4%–5% as panic liquidations subside; (2) Volume Dry-Up—down-day volume must fall well below the 224.75M 30-day average rather than printing 630M-share distribution spikes; (3) 4H Momentum Inflection—intraday_4h_turn must flip true via a higher low and reclaim of the 4H 20-EMA ($158.52 declining); and (4) Macro Breadth Stabilization—S&P 500 breadth >50DMA (currently 35.8%) must stop deteriorating.

Scenario Math on the Conditional Feb 2027 $125/$215 Call Spread: Across expiry scenarios on 2027-02-19, finishing at or below $125.00 results in the full -$1,612.00 max loss (-100% return on risk), whereas breakeven sits at $141.12 (+12.42% from CMP) and full max profit of +$7,388.00 (+458.3% return on risk) is achieved at or above $215.00. Profit-taking discipline targets closing at 65%–75% of max profit ($5,171.60 gain) before late-stage theta accelerates, or exiting immediately if NVDA closes below $124.50.

web_blocks.title: Stage 4 Rule: Never Average Down Into Active Institutional Liquidation
paragraphs: With 2.80x average volume on a -14.01% down day and 10 S&P 500 distribution days, institutional funds are actively cutting exposure following the SEC probe and CEO transition [23, 24].

Our technical gate (CAP_REJECTED) prohibits buying Stage 4 breakdowns. Wait for NVDA to either stabilize on the $124.50 shelf (for the capped $1,612 spread) or complete a multi-week Stage 1 base in the $105.00–$118.00 zone with a hard invalidation stop at $96.00.

book_paragraphs: If fundamental valuation tells you what a business is worth over a multi-year cycle, technical structure tells you what institutional capital is actually doing today. As of November 20, 2026, the tape on NVIDIA Corporation is unambiguous: the stock is locked in a violent Weinstein Stage 4 markdown. Closing at $125.53 after a 14.01 percent single-day collapse, NVIDIA has shed 26.12 percent in one week, 43.19 percent in one month, and 48.42 percent from its early-October 52-week high of $243.37. TradingView's -26.12% 1W and -43.19% 1M returns differ slightly from Finviz's trailing-window returns (-22.92% 1W / -40.85% 1M) due to window and cut-off convention. While the quantitative facts ledger tags NVDA Stage 1 (Basing) near its $124.50 low, stage2_evaluation classifies it STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN) below falling 50D, 200D, and 30W averages. Every major trend-following guardrail—the 20-day moving average at $181.46, the 50-day moving average at $207.00, the 200-day moving average at $203.35, the 10-week EMA at $188.46, and the 30-week SMA at $208.02—now sits 33 to 40 percent above the current share price as massive overhead supply.

This breakdown is occurring inside a hostile broader market. The S&P 500 sits in a confirmed Downtrend with 10 distribution days over the past 25 trading sessions. Only 35.8 percent of stocks trade above their 50-day moving average, and just 40.3 percent trade above their 200-day moving average. Across all eleven S&P sectors, only one holds above its 20-day average and three hold above their 50-day average. In that environment, institutional portfolio managers do not buy dips in high-beta semiconductor leaders facing governance and regulatory probes; they raise cash. On November 20 alone, 630.31 million shares of NVIDIA changed hands—2.80 times the 30-day average volume of 224.75 million shares—while short interest remained a modest 1.21 percent of float. That combination proves the selling is driven by long-only institutional de-risking rather than a short squeeze setup.

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Anatomy: Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour Exhaustion
paragraphs: Examining the 1W, 1D, and 4H timeframes together reveals why discipline demands standing aside at $125.53. On the weekly chart, NVIDIA's 14-week RSI has dropped to 25.01, and its 84.68 percent Bollinger bandwidth reflects extreme liquidation volatility rather than a tight, constructive Volatility Contraction Pattern. On the daily chart, the 14-day RSI sits at 15.05—a historically extreme oversold reading—while the 14-day Average True Range has expanded to $10.71, or 8.53 percent of the share price per day. The stock sliced through both Pivot S1 at $189.25 and Pivot S2 at $173.86 without pausing, leaving a wide air pocket overhead.

On the 4-hour chart, the intraday turn flag remains false. Price sits 20.81 percent below its 4-hour 20-EMA of $158.52 and 33.5 percent below its 4-hour 50-SMA of $188.79, with 4-hour RSI pinned at 14.95. While a 15-handle RSI can easily trigger a sharp, multi-day reflexive bounce off the $124.50 52-week low shelf, reflexive bounces inside Stage 4 downtrends routinely fail into overhead moving averages. A durable bottom requires weeks of sideways Stage 1 basing—where daily ATR compresses, liquidation volume dries up, and the stock builds a higher low in our $105.00 to $118.00 accumulation zone.

Short-interest data reinforces this reading. Only 279.58 million shares—just 1.21 percent of NVIDIA’s 23.19 billion share float, or 1.74 days to cover—are sold short. When a stock drops 43.19 percent in a month with minimal short interest, the pressure is overwhelmingly long-only institutional liquidation and mutual-fund/hedge-fund de-grossing rather than a temporary short raid that can snap back in a squeeze.

A closer look at the moving-average geometry underscores how much repair work lies ahead before NVIDIA can re-enter a Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend. At $125.53, the stock sits $55.93 below its 20-day simple moving average ($181.46), $77.82 below its 200-day simple moving average ($203.35), and $81.47 below its 50-day simple moving average ($207.00). On the weekly chart, the 10-week EMA ($188.46) has crossed decisively beneath the 30-week SMA ($208.02) and is sloping downward—a textbook Stage 4 signature.

Because overhead supply is stacked across every 10-point increment between $140 and $208, any initial rally off the $124.50 shelf will likely encounter heavy institutional selling from trapped October and November buyers looking to exit near breakeven. That is why professional trend followers do not buy the first bounce out of a Stage 4 waterfall. Instead, they allow trapped supply to churn sideways through time, letting the 20-day and 50-day averages flatten out before committing new equity capital.

Moreover, in a market environment where only 1 of 11 S&P 500 sectors trades above its 20-day moving average and 3 of 11 sit above their 50-day moving average, broad index correlations rise sharply during selloffs. Even fundamentally strong stocks struggle to sustain breakouts when institutional desks are raising cash across the board, reinforcing our decision to keep 100 percent of marginal capital in cash until NVDA completes its Stage 1 base.

book_subsections.title: The Conditional Options & Call-Convexity Overlay
paragraphs: For traders who want defined-risk upside exposure without risking full equity capital in a Stage 4 waterfall, our options desk evaluated the public February 19, 2027 chain (89 days to expiration; live Robinhood session was not open, so public chain mid-prices were used). Implied volatility is fair rather than panic-inflated, with at-the-money implied volatility at 66.9 percent versus 20-day historical volatility of 67.7 percent.

Even with fair implied volatility, buying outright calls at $125.53 is a trap because daily time decay accelerates rapidly if the stock chops sideways. Instead, our conditional playbook specifies a Bull Call Debit Spread: buying the February 19, 2027 $125 Call at $16.80 mid and selling the $215 Call at $0.68 mid for a net debit of $16.12 per share ($1,612.00 per contract, or 161.2 basis points of portfolio NAV). That $1,612.00 is the absolute maximum loss, while maximum profit reaches $7,388.00 (a 4.58-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio) at or above $215.00, with a breakeven of $141.12 (+12.42 percent). Selling the upper $215 strike cuts daily theta decay to -$7.52 per day while retaining +$53.30 of net delta per $1 move. Crucially, this spread is strictly conditional: deploy only if NVDA holds and stabilizes on the $124.50 shelf, and exit immediately on any daily close below $124.50.

Walking through the exact expiry payoff scenarios illustrates why this spread beats buying unhedged shares or naked calls during a high-uncertainty rebound. If NVIDIA closes at or below $125.00 on February 19, 2027, the spread expires worthless and your loss is strictly capped at the $1,612.00 upfront debit—161.2 basis points of portfolio NAV—regardless of whether the stock falls to $105.00 or $85.00. At $141.12 (+12.42 percent from the $125.53 close), the spread breaks even dollar-for-dollar at $1,612.00. If NVIDIA stages a relief rally to $215.00 (+71.3 percent) or overshoots to $245.00 (+95.2 percent), the spread reaches its full $9,000.00 intrinsic width, locking in +$7,388.00 net profit (+458.3 percent return on risk).

Equally important is active exit management before expiration. Rather than holding into the final weeks of February when time decay accelerates, our playbook targets closing the spread at 65 to 75 percent of maximum profit—roughly a $5,171.60 net gain—or exiting immediately if NVIDIA prints a daily close below the $124.50 major shelf. That combination of defined $1,612.00 risk and 4.58-to-1 upside convexity lets disciplined traders participate if $124.50 holds, without violating our Stage 4 equity ban.

For investors tracking institutional flow, the options market also provides a real-time sentiment gauge. On the February 19, 2027 expiration, open interest sits at 2,143 contracts on the $125 call strike and 6,218 contracts on the $215 call strike, with bid-ask spreads of $16.35 to $17.25 on the $125 call and $0.65 to $0.70 on the $215 call. That healthy liquidity allows disciplined limit-order execution near the $16.12 net debit mid-price without paying wide market-maker slippage—provided we adhere strictly to the $124.50 stabilization trigger.

book_subsections.title: Stage 1 Base-Building Checklist: What Confirms a Durable Bottom
paragraphs: In institutional trend-following, the transition from a Stage 4 markdown to a buyable Stage 1 base is never a single V-shaped candle; it is a multi-week process of supply absorption. For NVIDIA, lifting our CAP_REJECTED technical gate requires four concrete tape milestones. First, volatility must compress: a 14-day Average True Range of $10.71—representing 8.53 percent daily swings—and an 84.68 percent Bollinger bandwidth reflect unstable liquidation. Until daily ranges tighten toward 4 to 5 percent, any stop-loss placed inside normal noise risks being whipsawed.

Second, distribution volume must dry up. The 630.31 million shares traded on November 20—2.80 times the 30-day average—showed large institutions exiting indiscriminately. A true bottom forms when retests of the $105.00 to $118.00 demand zone occur on shrinking volume, signaling that forced sellers have exhausted their supply. Third, the 4-hour chart must print a higher low and reclaim its declining 20-period EMA, flipping our intraday turn indicator from false to true. Fourth, broader S&P 500 breadth (currently just 35.8 percent above 50-day moving averages with 10 distribution days) must stabilize so the macro tape stops dragging down every bounce.

Until these four conditions appear, both long-only equity buyers and unhedged call buyers are fighting institutional momentum. Patience is not passivity; it is waiting for the market to prove that $105.00 to $118.00 is an accumulation shelf rather than a trapdoor.

In summary, the technical verdict is unambiguous: NVIDIA’s Stage 4 breakdown—marked by a 15.05 daily RSI, 14.95 four-hour RSI, 25.01 weekly RSI, and 630.31 million shares of institutional distribution—demands patience. Keep equity capital sidelined until the four-part Stage 1 base-building checklist is satisfied in the $105.00 to $118.00 demand zone, and reserve the conditional $1,612.00 February 2027 $125/$215 Bull Call Spread strictly for a confirmed hold on the $124.50 shelf. With the S&P 500 in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend and only 35.8 percent of stocks above their 50-day moving averages, respecting the tape is the surest way to protect capital for the eventual Stage 2 recovery.
